summary: James Haughton Woods was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Harvard College and the University of Strasbourg, as well as under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held a post at Harvard University (~1903–1934).

James Irving Manatt was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, later holding posts at Denison College, Marietta College, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the United States, and Brown University (Professor, ~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Sonoma State University and the Pacific School of Religion. He studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman, Houn Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant, and founded Boundless Way Zen and Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indologist who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as Professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and as Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

James L. Taylor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields who completed his PhD at Macquarie University by 1989. He served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).
James Legge was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and Highbury College. He was appointed Professor at the University of Oxford in 1876.

James Leibold is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Southern California under Charlotte Furth. He has held academic posts at the University of Melbourne and La Trobe University.

James Luther Adams was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. He held a post at Harvard University from approximately 1956 to 1968.

James Mallinson is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Eton College, SOAS, and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS, Wolfson College, Oxford, and became Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford in 2023.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and as an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard, supervised by Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at the University of Southern California and Cornell University.

James Miller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who completed degrees at the University of Cambridge and Boston University. He was attested in 2014 as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University at Kingston.
James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler. He held an appointment as Librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Murdoch was a historian, archaeologist, and Japanologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen and under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Kanazawa University (~1893–1894), the University of Tokyo (~1898–1908), and Kagoshima University (~1908–1917).

James Prinsep was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He held positions at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and the Banaras Mint, became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1828, and directed The Asiatic Society from 1832 to 1838.

James Robert Ballantyne was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He served at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, headed Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and was librarian at the India Office.

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology educated at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford. He held posts at Williams College, the University of Michigan, Harvard University, and became director of the Harvard-Yenching Institute in 2024.

James Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and later as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).
